stem:
Chipo Sibanda sells farm equipment to smallholders around Marondera. She allows customers 30 days' credit. In 2025 she lowered her prices to win more customers. Extracts from her financial statements:

|  | 2024 US\$ | 2025 US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Revenue (all on credit) | 186,000 | 211,000 |
| Cost of sales | 122,760 | 145,590 |
| Expenses (including loan interest) | 41,100 | 46,420 |
| Loan interest | 2,100 | 2,100 |
| Inventory at 31 December (1 January 2024: 12,200) | 14,700 | 20,600 |
| Trade receivables | 15,800 | 23,120 |
| Bank | 4,300 | – |
| Bank overdraft | – | 3,700 |
| Trade payables | 9,900 | 14,100 |
| Capital at 31 December | 72,000 | 78,000 |
| 10% loan (repayable 2032) | 21,000 | 21,000 |

Ratios for 2024:

| Ratio (2024) | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Gross profit margin | 34.0% |
| Profit margin | 11.9% |
| Return on capital employed | 26.1% |
| Acid test ratio | 2.03 : 1 |
| Rate of inventory turnover | 9.1 times |
| Trade receivables turnover | 31 days |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the gross profit margin for 2025, to one decimal place.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit margin for 2025, to one decimal place.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the return on capital employed for 2025, to one decimal place.
parts.explanation: Profit before interest 18,990 + 2,100 = 21,090; capital employed 78,000 + 21,000 = 99,000; ROCE 21.3%.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Profit before interest 18,990 + 2,100 = 21,090; capital employed 78,000 + 21,000 = 99,000; ROCE 21.3%.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the acid test ratio at 31 December 2025, as x : 1 to two decimal places.
parts.explanation: Current assets 43,720 − inventory 20,600 = 23,120; current liabilities 17,800 (including the overdraft); 1.30 : 1.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Current assets 43,720 − inventory 20,600 = 23,120; current liabilities 17,800 (including the overdraft); 1.30 : 1.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the rate of inventory turnover for 2025, to one decimal place.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Calculate the trade receivables turnover in days for 2025, to the nearest whole day.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Comment on the change in Chipo's profitability between 2024 and 2025.

points.description: Gross margin fell from 34.0% to 31.0%, consistent with the price cuts
Profit margin fell from 11.9% to 9.0% and ROCE from 26.1% to 21.3%
Revenue rose by 13.4% but profit for the year fell from 22,140 to 18,990: higher volume did not make up for lower margins and higher expenses

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Profitability has worsened. The price cuts lowered the gross margin from 34.0% to 31.0%. Expenses also rose, so the profit margin fell from 11.9% to 9.0% and ROCE from 26.1% to 21.3%. Revenue grew by 13.4%, but profit for the year fell from US\$22,140 to US\$18,990.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Comment on Chipo's liquidity and her management of inventory and trade receivables in 2025.

points.description: Acid test fell from 2.03 : 1 to 1.30 : 1 and the bank balance became an overdraft
Inventory turnover slowed from 9.1 to 8.2 times: more cash tied up in equipment
Customers took 40 days against 30 allowed (31 days in 2024): weaker credit control

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Liquidity has weakened: the acid test fell from 2.03 : 1 to 1.30 : 1 and the bank is overdrawn. Inventory rose to US\$20,600 and turnover slowed to 8.2 times, while customers now take 40 days to pay instead of 31, well beyond the 30 days allowed. Cash is tied up in stock and debts.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Evaluate Chipo's decision to lower her prices in 2025. Advise her whether she should continue with the lower prices.

points.description: For: revenue and customer numbers increased; may build market share / loyalty for the future
Against: lower margins, lower profit and ROCE, weaker liquidity as more stock and debts are carried
Other considerations: non-financial factors (competition, customers' ability to pay, the farming season)
Justified conclusion, e.g. raise prices partly and tighten credit control, or keep low prices only if expenses and debts are controlled

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The lower prices did attract customers: revenue rose by about one-eighth, which may build loyalty among smallholders. But the extra sales were less profitable, so profit and ROCE fell, and Chipo now carries more stock and slower debts, leaving her overdrawn. Unless competitors are also cutting prices, she should restore part of the price cut, enforce her 30-day credit terms and reduce inventory; continuing as in 2025 would keep weakening both profit and cash.

parts.explanation: Two sides, a non-financial point and a justified conclusion.

explanation: 2025 ratios: gross margin 31.0%, profit margin 9.0%, ROCE 21.3%, acid test 1.30 : 1, inventory turnover 8.2 times, receivables 40 days (2024: 34.0%, 11.9%, 26.1%, 2.03 : 1, 9.1 times, 31 days).
hints: ROCE uses profit before interest and capital employed = capital + non-current liabilities.
The overdraft is a current liability; all sales are on credit.
